contexts.text: That they might induce others to loan them honours, gain, and reputation.
For the sake of the profit of gain or honour.

Thou shalt not be as a usurer () = that it shall be done from charity. A usurer = one who does what is good for the sake of gain; for a usurer entrusts money to another for the sake of usury, and brings aid to another for the sake of recompense...
From these things it is now evident what is represented by the usurers who took usury; namely, those who do what is good for the sake of gain. Illustrated.
Hence the understanding may gain some light concerning the forms of Heaven.
These things will gain some light in the Memorabilia which follow.
They at last acquire a sight like that of owls.
This arcanum will gain light in what follows.
After the things said to you have gained some light.
From that time this has lent a light.
By thefts... are also meant thefts not manifest, as unlawful interest and profits...
Who abstain from thefts, that is, from unlawful profits and interest.
The works of merchants are all evil, so long as they do not regard and thence do not shun as sins unlawful profits and unlawful interest. (Or, unlawful gains and unlawful profits.)
In order that this may gain some light, it shall be illustrated by comparisons.
